name: Waste Connections, Inc.
tagline: North America's third-largest integrated solid waste services company
hero_kpi_rationale: Adjusted EBITDA de 3,125 millions USD en 2025, en croissance de 7.7% d'une année à l'autre, reflétant une expansion de marge de 50 points de base à 33.0% du chiffre d'affaires, démontrant une rentabilité opérationnelle solide dans un environnement d'inflation modérée

kpis.explanation: Sum of all revenue streams including waste collection, transfer, disposal, resource recovery and E&P waste services
kpis.description: Total revenues increased 6.1% to $9.467 billion in 2025 from $8.920 billion in 2024, with acquisitions contributing $377.2 million and organic growth of 1.9%

kpis.explanation: Non-GAAP measure of operating profitability before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization adjustments
kpis.description: Adjusted EBITDA increased 7.7% to $3.125 billion in 2025 from $2.902 billion in 2024, representing 33.0% of revenue compared to 32.5% in 2024

kpis.name_en: Net Income Attributable to Waste Connections
kpis.explanation: Consolidated net income after all expenses, taxes, and impairments
kpis.description: Net income increased 74% to $1.077 billion in 2025 from $617.6 million in 2024, primarily due to lower impairments of $109.7 million versus $613.0 million in 2024

kpis.name_en: Adjusted Net Income Attributable to Waste Connections
kpis.explanation: Non-GAAP measure of net income excluding certain non-recurring or non-operating items
kpis.description: Adjusted net income increased 7.2% to $1.328 billion in 2025 from $1.239 billion in 2024

kpis.explanation: Adjusted EBITDA as a percentage of total revenues
kpis.description: Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 50 basis points to 33.0% in 2025 from 32.5% in 2024, driven by price-led organic growth exceeding cost inflation

kpis.explanation: Year-over-year revenue growth excluding acquisitions and divestitures impact
kpis.description: Organic revenue growth was 1.9% in 2025, driven by 2.3% solid waste internal growth from pricing increases of 6.4%, partially offset by volume declines of 2.8%

kpis.explanation: Year-over-year price increases achieved on waste collection and disposal services
kpis.description: Core pricing grew 6.5% in 2025, with offsets from lower materials and environmental surcharges of 0.1 percentage point, demonstrating strong pricing power

kpis.explanation: Year-over-year decline in collection volumes, primarily from intentional non-renewal of lower-margin contracts
kpis.description: Volumes decreased 2.8% due to intentional shedding of lower quality revenue through non-renewal of certain residential hauling contracts, demonstrating disciplined portfolio management

kpis.explanation: Total debt to adjusted EBITDA ratio, non-GAAP measure of financial leverage
kpis.description: Leverage ratio increased slightly from 2.67x at December 31, 2024 to 2.75x at December 31, 2025, within the target range of 2.5x-3.0x despite acquisition spending and share repurchases

kpis.explanation: Combination of cash dividends paid and share repurchases in the period
kpis.description: Total shareholder distributions of $839.3 million in 2025 comprised $333.8 million in dividends (up 10.4% to reflect 11.1% quarterly dividend increase) and $505.5 million in share repurchases of 2.8 million shares

kpis.explanation: Percentage increase in quarterly cash dividend per common share
kpis.description: Quarterly cash dividend increased 11.1% from $0.315 to $0.350 per common share in October 2025, reflecting confidence in future cash generation

stories_kpis.explanation: Impact of acquisitions closed during and after the prior year on incremental revenues
stories_kpis.description: Acquisitions closed during or subsequent to prior year contributed $377.2 million in incremental revenues in 2025, demonstrating continued execution of acquisition-based growth strategy

stories_kpis.explanation: Remaining borrowing capacity under the Revolving Credit Agreement maturing February 2029
stories_kpis.description: Available borrowing capacity of $581.1 million under the Revolving Credit Agreement (maturing February 2029) provides flexibility for acquisitions and operational needs

stories_kpis.explanation: Total debt that can be prepaid without penalty as of year-end
stories_kpis.description: Total prepayable debt outstanding of $2.2 billion at December 31, 2025, maintained within target leverage range despite shareholder returns

stories_kpis.explanation: Cash balance at year-end available for operations and strategic initiatives
stories_kpis.description: Cash balance decreased from $62.4 million at December 31, 2024 to $46.0 million at December 31, 2025, reflecting deployment of capital toward acquisitions and shareholder returns

ai_positioning.summary: Waste Connections, Inc. does not mention artificial intelligence or machine learning in its Form 10-K filing. The company's focus remains on traditional waste management operations, vertical integration, and acquisition-based growth strategies.

risks.title: Competition
risks.score_rationale: The company operates in a highly competitive solid waste market where it competes primarily on price and secondarily on service quality. The industry has consolidated but remains fragmented with local competition in target markets. Multiple operators compete for landfill and collection contracts based on tipping fees, geographic location and operational efficiency.
risks.summary: Intense price competition in solid waste collection and disposal could pressure margins if the company cannot maintain pricing discipline or lose market share through customer churn.

risks.title: Regulatory and Environmental Compliance
risks.score_rationale: Changes in environmental regulations and legislative requirements can significantly increase operating costs and capital expenditures. The company faces ongoing compliance with landfill regulations, closure and post-closure obligations that are complex and costly. The MD&A explicitly mentions that regulatory changes related to landfill operations could have material adverse effects on financial performance.
risks.summary: Environmental regulations, landfill closure requirements and post-closure liability obligations could materially increase operating costs and impact financial results.

risks.title: Landfill Development and Closure Costs
risks.score_rationale: Landfill development and closure costs depend on future events and actual costs can differ materially from estimates. Reductions in landfill remaining life or increases in closure and post-closure cost estimates could negatively impact cash flows. The company must continuously develop new disposal capacity as existing landfills approach closure.
risks.summary: Unexpected increases in landfill development costs or accelerated closure timelines could reduce free cash flow and require higher capital deployment.

risks.title: Landfill Closure and Post-Closure Liabilities
risks.score_rationale: The company maintains significant obligations for landfill closure and post-closure monitoring that can span decades. Material increases in cost estimates or reductions in remaining landfill life could have material adverse impacts. These long-tail liabilities represent contingent obligations that could impact shareholder returns.
risks.summary: Significant closure and post-closure remediation liabilities could require substantial capital deployment or reduce available funds for shareholder distributions.

risks.title: Cybersecurity and Technology Risk
risks.score_rationale: The company depends on technology systems for operations including fleet management, billing and customer service. Cybersecurity threats could disrupt operations or compromise customer data. While the company maintains insurance including cyber liability coverage, a major breach could still impact operations and reputation.
risks.summary: Cybersecurity incidents could disrupt waste collection operations, compromise customer data or require significant remediation costs.

risks.title: Inflation and Cost Escalation
risks.score_rationale: The company faces cost inflation in fuel, labor, equipment and landfill development. While pricing increases of 6.4% in 2025 offset some inflation, wage escalation and fuel volatility could compress margins. Continued inflation could exceed the company's ability to raise prices without losing volumes.
risks.summary: Inflation in labor, fuel and materials costs could exceed pricing increases and compress operating margins if not offset by volume growth or further price increases.

risks.title: Labor and Workforce Challenges
risks.score_rationale: As a labor-intensive business, the company faces ongoing challenges in labor union negotiations, wage inflation and employee retention. The waste industry has historically experienced labor union activity and wage pressure. These costs could escalate faster than pricing increases.
risks.summary: Labor cost inflation and union negotiations could put pressure on operating margins and profitability if pricing increases cannot keep pace.
